developer: Heaviside LLC (Google development entity); Google LLC on the state contract
project: Google Cedar Rapids campus, 76th Avenue SW and Edgewood Road SW

documents.title: Iowa Economic Development Authority assistance contract 24-HQJP-014 (scanned)
The Gazette: council signs off on unnamed company's $576 million data center
Business Record: IEDA approves $56M local tax break

community_fund.controlled_by: The City, at its discretion; the company gets input.
community_fund.notes: Community Betterment Fund: $400,000 a year per data center building from the January 1 after occupancy, for 15 years or $6M per building, capped at $36M in total. Press reports of $350,000 are wrong; the executed agreement says $400,000.

clawbacks.notes: The exemption ceases prospectively if conditions lapse after a 60-day cure, and the franchise-fee rebate is skipped for any year of job noncompliance. The state contract lets IEDA revoke or reduce incentives after a 30-day cure, with layoffs or Iowa closures as default triggers. Meeting the investment minimum is a condition precedent to the exemption. No trigger tied to the facility ceasing operation after the job-maintenance window closes in 2033.

grid_costs.governed_by: Alliant Energy individual customer rate for 25 MW-plus customers; terms not public
grid_costs.notes: The agreement is silent on electric costs. Alliant's 2024 filings described up to 300 MW of new load potential.

water.notes: The City reserves water capacity for the property per an exhibit that is not in the posted PDF. A gray-water credit of $1.30 per hundred cubic feet, escalating 2.5 percent a year and capped at 57 percent of the sewer rate, applies to separately piped cooling discharge between 0.1 and 1.5 million gallons a day, with monthly reporting only if the credit is claimed. The utilities director says Google plans no water for cooling; 2024 estimates ranged from 200,000 to 7.8 million gallons a day. Google gave $1.3M toward a $12M to $14M aquifer storage well.

jobs.notes: 31 full-time jobs at $31.44 an hour by March 31, 2031, maintained through March 31, 2033, enforceable through the state contract and the city exemption conditions. No local hire and no prevailing wage.

local_contracting.notes: No local contracting or road repair term. A 75 percent rebate of electric franchise fees for 20 years per data center runs the other direction.

transparency.notes: The City signed a nondisclosure agreement with Google, disclosed through a records request in July 2026. The company was unnamed when the council approved the deal. The agreement has a confidentiality clause subject to open records law and a memorandum was recorded with the county. A council member complained little was shared on water, energy, or rate impacts.

tax.notes: 70 percent exemption on value added for 20 years under Iowa's High Quality Jobs program, starting the January 1 after the first building completes, plus a 75 percent franchise-fee rebate. The state contract estimates the local property tax exemption at $56,000,000 and awarded no state tax credits. No but-for analysis was found.

sources.where: Section 3.1, p. 7 and Exhibit B-1, p. 28

criticisms.summary: The company was not named when the council voted, and the City had signed an NDA.
Water-use estimates ranged from 200,000 to 7.8 million gallons a day at the time of approval.
